blog_summary: The blog post discusses the Spark Streaming paper by Zaharia et al. (2013), which introduces Discretized Streams (D-Streams) to address challenges in fault tolerance and straggler handling for large-scale stream processing. Traditional continuous operator models rely on replication or upstream backup for recovery, both of which are inefficient in large clusters—replication incurs 2× hardware costs, while upstream backup leads to slow recovery due to serial state rebuilding. D-Streams overcome these limitations by structuring streaming computations as a series of stateless, deterministic batch computations using Resilient Distributed Datasets (RDDs), which maintain data lineage for recovery without replication. This approach achieves sub-second end-to-end latencies and sub-second recovery times, making it suitable for applications like social media trend analysis, monitoring, and spam detection. The authors demonstrate linear scalability up to 100 nodes, processing over 60M records/second with per-node throughput comparable to commercial streaming databases. The D-Streams model also enables seamless integration with batch and interactive queries, enhancing Spark's versatility.
